noah: Heads up: I hit a weird pyright/mypy combo when using autogen dataclasses with kw_only=True. Minimal repro below.

noah: repro:
```py
from sampleapp import GeneratedModel
# GeneratedModel is dataclass with kw_only=True, tags: Optional[List[str]] = None
GeneratedModel("id", tags=None)  # works at runtime
# pyright: Too many positional arguments for "GeneratedModel"
# mypy: error about argument 1 type mismatch
```

vera: ah yeah I've seen that. Some editors infer the runtime __init__ differently for kw_only dataclasses and show positional errors.

oli: two fixes: change generator to not set kw_only for back-compat, or emit explicit __init__ signature (with Optional types) so static checkers see the same shape as runtime.

noah: I prefer keeping kw_only to avoid accidental positional args, but we should make typing accurate. Emitting an explicit __init__ in the generated class seems reasonable.

vera: Also add a tiny test in sampleapp CI that runs pyright in watch mode to catch these editor-only mismatches.

type-bot: Created issue #412: "generator: emit explicit __init__ for kw_only dataclasses to satisfy static checkers". CC @noah @vera @oli.

oli: I'll prototype a generator change that writes a small __init__ with Optional[...] parameters and then delegates to dataclass machinery. Will link PR soon.

noah: awesome, thanks. this will solve a couple of onboarding surprises for new users.
